facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies cross-user file read/update/delete or file access through file_id and explains that shared-chat/file access is not scoped to the requesting user or requested permission.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable shared-chat branch grants access if any shared chat references the file, without checking whether the requesting user can access that shared chat or whether the requested operation is read/write/delete.
facts.security_invariant: File access through shared chats must be scoped to the requesting user and requested access type.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies API key deletion by user-controlled id and explains that the delete operation is not scoped to the requesting user or ownership.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable deletion path accepted an API key identifier without verifying that the key belonged to the caller before deleting it.
facts.security_invariant: API key deletion must be scoped to the requesting user's ownership or permissions.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies nutritional value retrieval through the API and explains that the queryset/direct lookup is not scoped to the requesting user.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable view performed direct ORM access for nutritional values without applying the caller's user scope, allowing cross-user dietary data reads.
facts.security_invariant: Nutrition value API results must be scoped to data owned by or visible to the requesting user.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies routine or workout data access where cache keys or lookups are not scoped to the requesting user.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable routine API used cache keys or helper lookups that were not user-scoped, allowing one user to retrieve another user's workout routine data.
facts.security_invariant: Routine API actions and cache keys must be scoped to the requesting user.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies addon API enumeration or retrieval and explains that project/component access is missing or not applied to the queryset.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable API exposed addon configurations without enforcing project/component access control for the caller.
facts.security_invariant: Addon API results must be filtered to addon configurations visible to the requesting user.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies the /user/search/ endpoint and explains that authentication/authorization is missing or insufficient, or that user enumeration is possible without proper context (event/category) scoping.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable endpoint allows any authenticated user to dump user details (name, email, affiliation) via /user/search/ without verifying context permissions.
facts.security_invariant: User search endpoint must require an authorization token scoped to event/category managers.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies the Notion OAuth/indexing flow and explains that the external resource binding is not scoped to the authenticated user.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable Notion OAuth flow allowed a user-controlled identifier to bind or poison another user's Notion indexing context without checking ownership.
facts.security_invariant: Notion OAuth callbacks and indexing actions must bind the external account/workspace to the authenticated Khoj user.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies cached/exported file access by identifier and explains that the file's owning event/user authorization is missing or insufficient.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable file access path allowed cross-user or cross-event file access through UUID-like cached file references without sufficient ownership checks.
facts.security_invariant: Cached/exported files must only be readable by users authorized for the owning event or object.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies admin preview access and explains that preview content is reachable without the required object-level permission.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable preview views allowed improper access to preview content without fully checking the caller's permissions on the target object.
facts.security_invariant: Admin preview endpoints must enforce the same edit/view permission checks as the underlying page or snippet object.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies the execution stop endpoint and explains that an execution id can be stopped without verifying that the execution belongs to a workflow accessible to the caller.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable stop path passed only the user-controlled execution id to the service, which loaded the execution by id without filtering by the caller's accessible workflow ids.
facts.security_invariant: Stopping an execution must be scoped to executions belonging to workflows the requesting user can access.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies Puck CRUD/version/restore endpoints using Payload local API without enforcing collection access via req and overrideAccess: false.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable handlers called Payload local API methods without req and overrideAccess: false, causing the default overrideAccess behavior to bypass collection-level read, create, update, delete, version, and restore access checks.
facts.security_invariant: Puck API handlers must forward the current request and disable Payload local API access override so collection access rules are evaluated for the caller.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies Strapi document-service or content API queries accepting user-controlled lookup parameters and explains that lookup can filter on private fields or related admin-user fields before authorization/sanitization blocks access.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable document service accepted a user-controlled lookup parameter and applied it before private-field sanitization, allowing unauthenticated or low-privilege callers to infer private fields such as admin password hashes or reset tokens through filtering behavior.
facts.security_invariant: Public document-service queries must not accept internal lookup parameters that can filter on private fields or related admin-user fields.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies direct REST access to _Join relation tables and explains that non-master callers can create, update, delete, or read relation rows such as role memberships without the required authorization.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable REST enforcement did not block direct _Join: class operations, allowing clients to write _Join:users:_Role rows and alter role membership or bypass relation access controls.
facts.security_invariant: Internal _Join relation tables must not be directly read or mutated by normal clients; relation changes must go through authorized relation APIs or master/maintenance privileges.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies Langflow flow read/update/delete by flow_id (GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/flows/{flow_id}) and explains that the _read_flow helper does not unconditionally scope the database query to the authenticated user's ownership. A finding is stronger (and should be preferred) when it identifies the specific root cause: the Flow.user_id filter is applied only inside the `if auth_settings.AUTO_LOGIN:` branch, so when AUTO_LOGIN is False (authentication enabled, multi-user) no ownership filter is applied and any flow can be read, updated, or deleted by its UUID. A finding that correctly describes the missing per-user ownership scoping on _read_flow but does not name AUTO_LOGIN still matches.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable _read_flow helper queried by flow_id without unconditionally filtering by Flow.user_id, allowing authenticated users to read, modify, or delete another user's flow.
facts.security_invariant: Flow read, update, and delete operations must be scoped to flows owned by the requesting user.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies the image download endpoint and explains that unauthenticated or cross-user callers can retrieve images because flow ownership is not checked.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable image download route accepted a bare flow_id path parameter and served image files without requiring authentication or resolving the flow through the ownership-checking get_flow dependency.
facts.security_invariant: Image downloads for flow files must authenticate the caller and enforce ownership of the referenced flow.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies Weblate translation memory API write endpoints and explains that unintended create/update API operations are exposed without the required authorization.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable translation memory API used a writable model viewset surface for endpoints that were not intended to allow editing or creation, exposing operations without proper access control.
facts.security_invariant: Translation memory API endpoints must expose only the intended operations and must not permit unauthorized create or update operations.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies MLflow logged-model artifact download/list endpoints and explains that model read authorization is missing or not applied to the AJAX artifact route.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable AJAX artifact download route was not covered by the logged-model authorization validators, allowing users without model permission to access artifact files by model_id.
facts.security_invariant: Logged-model artifact download and listing endpoints must enforce read permission on the referenced logged model.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies Weblate's user or notification API and explains that listing/searching users or reading notification subscriptions is not restricted to the target user or callers with user-management permissions.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable API allowed user listing/search and notification subscription reads without a target-user authorization check, so a caller could enumerate users or fetch notification settings for another username or subscription id.
facts.security_invariant: User-management and notification API reads must be scoped to the requesting user's own account or to callers with user view/edit permissions; unauthenticated or low-privileged callers must not enumerate users or retrieve another user's notification subscriptions.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies Flowise DocumentStore create or update accepting client-controlled id/workspaceId/internal fields and explains that repository.save or mass assignment can overwrite or reassign another workspace's DocumentStore without object/workspace authorization.
facts.invariant_violation: The vulnerable create path mass-assigned the request body into a DocumentStore entity and persisted it with TypeORM save(), allowing a client-supplied id to turn create into an implicit upsert and potentially overwrite or reassign DocumentStores across workspaces.
facts.security_invariant: DocumentStore create and update paths must ignore client-controlled primary keys, workspaceId, timestamps, and internal state fields, and must bind the object to the authenticated user's active workspace server-side.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A true match must point at the run-creation path in libs/aegra-api/src/aegra_api/api/runs.py (create_run / create_and_stream_run / wait_for_run, or the shared _prepare_run call) and identify the missing thread-ownership check (caller-supplied thread_id used without comparing the thread's user_id to the authenticated user.identity), not merely flag the read endpoints or the @auth.on hook.
facts.invariant_violation: POST /threads/{thread_id}/runs, /runs/stream, and /runs/wait pass the caller-supplied thread_id straight into _prepare_run with no thread-ownership check (handle_event is default-allow when no @auth.on handler is registered, and stream/wait do not call it at all), so any authenticated user can execute runs against, read checkpoint state from, and inject messages into another user's thread.
facts.security_invariant: Before creating/streaming/waiting a run for a caller-supplied thread_id, the server must verify the thread is owned by the authenticated user (thread.user_id == user.identity) at the SQL layer, returning 404 if owned by another user.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies that POST /studiocms_api/dashboard/update-user-notifications (handler updateUserNotifications) uses the payload-supplied `id` as the update target rather than the authenticated session user id (userData.user.id), and explains that it only checks login/visitor level with no ownership-or-admin check, allowing one authenticated user to modify another user's notification preferences.
facts.invariant_violation: The updateUserNotifications handler takes the target user id from the request payload and passes it directly to sdk.GET.users.byId and sdk.AUTH.user.update after only verifying the caller is a logged-in visitor, so any authenticated user can overwrite any other user's notification preferences.
facts.security_invariant: A user may only modify their own notification preferences; the target user id must equal the authenticated caller's session user id unless the caller is an admin.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies that a git push to git-receive-pack can carry commits not within the approved commitFrom..commitTo range (new-branch / zero-hash handling in parsePush.ts/getDiff.ts) and that the push-action chain lacks a check ensuring all pack commits are within the introduced/approved range, allowing unapproved commits to bypass the approval gate.
facts.invariant_violation: For a new-branch (zero-hash) push, parsePush.ts rewrites commitFrom to the last commit's parent and getDiff.ts diffs only that introduced window, while the push-action chain has no step verifying the pack contains only approved/introduced commits, so an attacker who branches off an unapproved commit can get the child branch approved and then push the unapproved parent-branch commit past the approval gate to the remote.
facts.security_invariant: On a git push, every commit object contained in the received pack must lie within the introduced (oldOid..newOid) range that the approval gate (checkIfWaitingAuth/blockForAuth) actually authorized; commits not reachable in that range must not be proxied to the upstream remote without their own approval.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A true match points at packages/sync-server/src/app-sync.ts and identifies that one or more of the 8 /sync/* file handlers fetch the file by caller-supplied id (verifyFileExists / FilesService.get) without checking file.owner === res.locals.user_id (nor isAdmin / countUserAccess) before reading or mutating it. Findings that only flag the already-guarded /sync/delete-user-file, or that point elsewhere in the monorepo, do not match.
facts.invariant_violation: The 8 sync handlers call verifyFileExists/FilesService.get(fileId), which only confirms the file exists by id and performs no owner scoping, then proceed to read/overwrite/reset/rename the file or its encryption keys — so any authenticated user in multi-user (OpenID) mode acts on any other user's file by supplying its id (BOLA/IDOR).
facts.security_invariant: Every /sync/* endpoint that operates on a budget file must verify the authenticated user (res.locals.user_id) owns the file (file.owner === userId), is a server admin (isAdmin), or has been granted access (user_access) before reading or mutating it.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A true match must identify that the POST and/or DELETE /api/scheduler handler in server/api/scheduler/index.js performs a state-changing scheduler mutation while enforcing only a guest check (isGuestUser) and omitting the administrator authorization check (haveAdminPermission / checkGroupsFnc), allowing a non-admin authenticated operator to reach admin-only scheduled device-write and script-execution functionality. Pointing only at the mount file (server/api/index.js) or at a guest-only check is insufficient.
facts.invariant_violation: At the vulnerable commit the POST and DELETE /api/scheduler handlers gate only on authJwt.isGuestUser(); they never compute permission via checkGroupsFnc nor call haveAdminPermission, so an authenticated non-admin operator can create, modify, or delete scheduled actions that execute privileged PLC writes (setTagValue) and server-side scripts (runScript) — operator-to-admin function-level escalation.
facts.security_invariant: Mutating /api/scheduler endpoints (POST create/modify, DELETE) must require administrator permission via authJwt.haveAdminPermission(checkGroupsFnc(req)), matching every other write endpoint that reaches runtime.devices.setTagValue or runtime.scriptsMgr.runScript.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies that the /tenant/create authorization (create_tenant_allowed) evaluates the caller's role in the tenant schema context rather than the root context, allowing a logged-in tenant admin to create a tenant on the root domain; bonus if it notes the missing root-schema (db.getTenantSchema() === default_schema) check or that role_to_create_tenant is not enforced cross-context.
facts.invariant_violation: create_tenant_allowed evaluates the caller's role from req.user.role_id in the CURRENT tenant's schema context and never checks that the request is on the root schema, so a tenant admin (low role_id within their own tenant) passes the check and creates a new tenant on the root domain's public schema - cross-context vertical privilege escalation.
facts.security_invariant: Creating a tenant on the root domain must be authorized using the role evaluated in the ROOT schema context (and only when the request is served from the root/default schema, or the configured create role is the public role 100).

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies the polls.comments.delete tRPC mutation (HTTP POST /api/trpc/polls.comments.delete) deleting a comment selected only by user-supplied commentId without verifying the requester is the comment author (userId/guestId) or has poll admin access. It must flag the missing ownership/authorization check before the delete, not merely the presence of a delete operation.
facts.invariant_violation: The delete mutation looks up the comment solely by client-supplied commentId and deletes it with no ownership or poll-admin check, so any authenticated or guest user can delete any comment by id.
facts.security_invariant: Only the comment's author (matching userId or guestId) or a user with poll admin access may delete a comment.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies the shares.create handler (server/routes/api/shares/shares.ts) and reports that the authorization check only validates the collection (the collectionId ? collection : document ternary) while ignoring the user-supplied documentId, enabling an IDOR / cross-tenant share of arbitrary documents. Reporting the documents.info exfiltration path strengthens but is not required.
facts.invariant_violation: When both collectionId and documentId are supplied, shares.create authorizes only the collection via the ternary authorize(user, "read", collectionId ? collection : document) and never authorizes the document, allowing an authenticated user to mint a public share link for any document on the instance (including documents in other workspaces) and exfiltrate its contents via documents.info using the shareId.
facts.security_invariant: To create a share for a document, the requesting user must be authorized to read (and, when publishing, share) that specific document; authorization must validate the document object itself, not a sibling collection.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies that RecipeViewSet.batch_update (PUT /api/recipe/batch_update/) lacks per-object authorization: its queryset filters by space only and omits the private/created_by/shared check, allowing modification of other users' private recipes. Noting that the detail=False action skips has_object_permission, and that shared_add/private enable self-grant or forced exposure, strengthens the match.
facts.invariant_violation: The detail=False batch_update action never triggers DRF has_object_permission; its queryset filters recipes by space=request.space only, so any authenticated Space user can modify (and self-grant access to or un-private) any recipe in the Space, including other users' private recipes.
facts.security_invariant: A user may only modify a private recipe in their Space if they are its creator or in its shared list; the object-level authorization enforced on PUT /api/recipe/{id}/ must hold equally for the batch_update action.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it flags missing workspace-membership authorization on WorkspaceFileAssetEndpoint (one or more of post/patch/delete/get reachable via /api/assets/v2/workspaces/<slug>/...), and/or the unscoped source-asset lookup in DuplicateAssetEndpoint that omits source-workspace authorization. Generic 'missing auth' without tying it to the workspace-slug/asset cross-tenant boundary is insufficient.
facts.invariant_violation: WorkspaceFileAssetEndpoint's post/patch/delete/get methods carry no allow_permission decorator (BaseAPIView requires only IsAuthenticated), so any authenticated user can operate on any workspace's assets by supplying the target slug/asset UUID; DuplicateAssetEndpoint authorizes only the destination workspace and loads the source asset by raw UUID with no source-workspace authorization.
facts.security_invariant: A user may only read, create, patch, or delete a workspace's V2 assets (and may only duplicate a source asset) if they are an active member of that workspace, enforced via the WORKSPACE-level allow_permission / WorkspaceMember membership check.

facts.evaluation_match_criteria: A finding matches if it identifies that the admin_or_owner_required decorator in askbot/views/avatar_views.py fails to authorize because it compares request.user.id (int) against the string user_id taken from the URL, so ownership never matches and control falls through to login_required, letting any authenticated user act on another user's avatars via /avatar/*/<user_id>/. The fix coerces user_id to int and denies with HttpResponseForbidden. Findings about the separate avatar delete path (keyed on avatar_id, which has its own ownership check), about authentication, or about output escaping are not matches.
facts.invariant_violation: The admin_or_owner_required decorator compares request.user.id (an int) to the user_id URL kwarg, which Django passes as a string from the (?P<user_id>\d+) regex, so request.user.id == user_id is always False even for the legitimate owner. The non-matching branch then falls through to login_required(func), which succeeds for ANY authenticated user, so an attacker who substitutes a victim's user_id can upload, set-primary, or enable/reset avatars on another user's account.
facts.security_invariant: Only the account owner (request.user.id equal to the target user_id) or a site administrator may view or modify a given user's avatars/profile picture; any other authenticated user must be denied.
